text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High-rate GPU driver resets observed across eu-west serving nodes (Xid events). Paging oncall.

jin: seeing repeating driver reset logs from node gpu-eu-07, looks like kernel reports: 'NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31'

tyler: same on gpu-eu-08 and gpu-eu-09. Pods running runtime-infer are restarting, a few OOMs as the container crashes right after driver reset.

maria: any customer impact yet?

support-ops: support telemetry: ~120 failed requests over last 5m, elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate for some Dedicated tenants in eu-west. CS queue has 2 tickets (acct: stromx & softlens).

jin: attaching tail of dmesg from gpu-eu-07:

```
Mar 15 12:02:11 gpu-eu-07 kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, pid=4123
Mar 15 12:02:11 gpu-eu-07 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31 detected on GPU 0
Mar 15 12:02:12 kubelet[...]: Container runtime pod runtime-infer-xx exited with status 137
Mar 15 12:02:12 kubelet[...]: Evicted pod runtime-infer-xx due to OOMKilled
```

ash: 31 is often memory corruption / ECC related but can be triggered by driver issues too. What's the ECC count?

jin: ECC counters show a small spike, not sustained. PCIe link errors also small but correlated.

tyler: immediate mitigations I propose: cordon + drain gpu-eu-07/08, scale up a reserve pool in us-west to absorb traffic, enable fallback model (cpu variant) for affected Dedicated customers to prevent 5xx.

maria: agree. Do we have capacity to shift? We have 2 spare general-purpose nodes in us-west pool but they are CPU only; latency will increase but better than errors.

support-ops: notifying Acct owners: message prepared -> "We are investigating GPU instability in EU; short-term we may route requests to CPU-backed fallback causing elevated latency. We'll update in 15m."

jen (typo correction): jin: ping on whether to escalate to infra/warranty for potential hardware replacement?

jin: holding off until we confirm persistent ECC. For now drain and observe. I'll trigger cordon+drain on the two worst nodes.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: scale runtime-infer replica count -> from 40 to 60 in eu cluster (safe-stagger).

ash: when draining, use --ignore-daemonsets and set grace to 120s. Also set node annotation: incident/gpu-flicker=true so monitoring picks it up.

tyler: comand i'm running:

```
kubectl cordon gpu-eu-07
kubectl drain gpu-eu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
kubectl cordon gpu-eu-08
kubectl drain gpu-eu-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

jin: after drain: pods moved, but one node gpu-eu-09 started showing repeated Xid 79 errors and a kernel oops, causing kubelet restarts. I'm pulling node logs now.

maria: that means it's spreading. Is there a recent kernel/driver rollout?

tyler: no driver change in last 7d. We did push a model container change yesterday but should be process-local.

ash: could be a temperature/power transient — check thermals and power rails on the hardware. Also check miner / hw management for fan speed.

jin: thermal sensors are normal; fans good. nv-hostengine shows a few ECC single-bit corrected counts increased around the first crash window.

support-ops: I've emailed the two affected customers with an ETA and mitigation steps. CS will offer SLA credit if persistent.

tyler: short-term additional mitigation: enable runtime fallback routing at the gateway for Dedicated eu-west -> route to cpu-fallback for accounts showing error spikes. This reduces failed requests.

maria: confirm full scope in 10m then we'll decide whether to escalate to replacements and to involve supply chain for potential RMA. Also need a post-incident timeline.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: oncall shift change in 45m. New oncall: ash will take lead.

ash: taking lead. Summary: active GPU driver resets (Xid 31/79) across eu-west GPU nodes -> causing container crashes and some OOMs. Immediate actions done: cordoned/drained two nodes, scaled replicas, enabled CPU fallback routing for affected Dedicated customers, support notified. Next steps: continue to drain noisy nodes, gather ECC counters, capture nvidia-smi -q, and check whether behavior continues on nodes after reboot. If noisy after reboot, RMA.

jin: I'll collect nvidia-smi -q, nvml logs, and sysfs ECC counters and drop them in /incident/artifacts/2112345678.

tyler: also enabling temporary increased retry/backoff at the API gateway to reduce pressure.

maria: logging this as 'gpu-node-flicker-2112345678' and assigning to infra for hardware follow-up.

support-ops: CS updated customers with current mitigation: fallbacks in place, latency expected +300-800ms, error rate reduced by ~70% after routing.

ash: if we see reoccurrence after restarting nvidia driver, escalate to on-call infra-hardware and open an RMA. If it stops, we'll keep nodes cordoned for 2h and then return to service one-by-one with smoke tests.

jin: quick commands I'm running now to gather state:

```
nvidia-smi -q > /incident/artifacts/2112345678/gpu-eu-07-smi.txt
cat /var/log/kern.log | grep -i nvrm > /incident/artifacts/2112345678/gpu-eu-07-kern.txt
for n in gpu-eu-07 gpu-eu-08 gpu-eu-09; do ssh $n 'cat /sys/class/pci_bus/0000:03/device/ec_* 2>/dev/null' > /incident/artifacts/$n-ecc.txt; done
```

deploy-bot: autoscaler: temporary pool created: eu-west-cpu-fallback-01 (3 nodes).

ash: I'm taking over the follow-up; if anyone finds permanent ECC multi-bit or persistent kernel oops after reboots, ping infra-hardware and move to RMA. Handoff note: ash -> next oncall in 4h is tyler.

support-ops: filing incident ticket INC-2112345678 with summary and customer impact numbers.

maria: thanks team. Will circle back in 30m with updated impact and next steps.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: status -> mitigation in place. Monitoring: working.

[end of thread]
